clue.text: Design new exercise in bowling

indicators.note: new says the letters of the word before it are made afresh in a different order

parts.note: PE is physical education, school exercise

explanation.surface: A fresh routine of physical training is introduced into a cricket bowler's work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges DESIGN with PE to make the answer; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Bowling along means travelling fast, so bowling can stand for going too fast on the road.

clue.text: Fasten lead round old dummy?

indicators.note: round says the lead's symbol goes around the word for fasten

parts.note: Pb is the chemical symbol for lead
to lace is to fasten, as shoes

explanation.surface: Someone ties a lead round an old tailor's dummy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lead' is the metal, not a dog's leash; 'round' is the containment signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A placebo is a dummy pill with no active drug, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Explorers primarily head into unknowns not listed

indicators.note: primarily asks for the first letter of the word explorers
into says the word for head goes inside the pair of unknowns

parts.note: x and y are the usual unknowns in algebra
a director is the head of a company

explanation.surface: The leading explorers venture into uncharted territory that appears on no map.
explanation.walkthrough: EX-DIRECTORY is the British term for a telephone number deliberately left out of the phone book.
explanation.definitionFit: An ex-directory telephone number is deliberately not listed in the phone book.

clue.text: Bull's penned in by this topless reprobate

indicators.note: topless means the first letter of the word for reprobate is removed

parts.note: a sinner is a reprobate, a wicked person

explanation.surface: A bull is shut in a pen by some shameless rogue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'topless' drops the S of SINNER. On a target the bull's-eye is ringed by the inner circle, so the bull is penned in by it.
explanation.definitionFit: On an archery or darts target, the inner ring immediately encircles the central bull.

clue.text: Device finally securing Michael's introduction?

indicators.note: finally asks for the last letter of the word securing

parts.note: a man called Michael introducing himself might say I'm Mick

explanation.surface: A gadget is the last piece needed to secure an introduction to Michael.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally' gives G from securing; Michael introducing himself says 'I'm Mick', IMMICK.
explanation.definitionFit: A gimmick is a device or trick meant to attract attention.

clue.text: Stone serpent buried in clod? Nearly

indicators.note: buried in says the serpent sits inside the shortened word for clod
nearly means the word for clod loses its final letter

parts.note: a jerk is a clod, a stupid person
an asp is a venomous snake

explanation.surface: A snake lies almost buried in a clump of earth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clod' looks like a lump of soil but means a dolt; 'Nearly' drops its last letter before 'buried in' takes the snake.
explanation.definitionFit: Jasper is an opaque, often red, semi-precious stone.

clue.text: Ball put on vessel for old swinger

parts.note: the jack is the small target ball in bowls
a ketch is a two-masted sailing vessel

explanation.surface: A ball is loaded onto a ship for an ageing playboy.
explanation.walkthrough: JACK KETCH was a notorious 17th-century English hangman, whose name became a byword for the executioner; his victims swung.
explanation.definitionFit: Jack Ketch was an old English public hangman, someone who made people swing from the gallows.

clue.text: To do sport is the end for so many Russians

definitions.meaning: to glide over snow on runners is a winter sport

definitions.text: the end for so many Russians
definitions.meaning: many Russian surnames end in these three letters, as in Tchaikovsky

explanation.surface: Playing games is the finish for countless Russians.
explanation.definitionFit: Skiing is a sport, and the same letters close countless Slavic surnames such as Nijinski.

clue.text: Girl cut public school fencing team

indicators.note: fencing means the school's name encloses the shortened girl's name

parts.note: Eton is the famous English public school

indicators.note: cut means the girl's name loses its last letter

parts.note: Vera is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl has been dropped from her public school's fencing team.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fencing' looks like the sport but means enclosing. EVERTON is a Liverpool football club.
explanation.definitionFit: Everton is a Premier League football club from Liverpool, so it is a team.

clue.text: Whisk handmade icing in summer

indicators.note: to whisk is to beat and stir, so these letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A cook whips up home-made icing during the summer months.
explanation.walkthrough: 'summer' is not the season but one who sums.
explanation.definitionFit: An adding machine sums figures, so it is a summer in the sense of one that adds.

clue.text: Originally translated mistake as rogue

indicators.note: originally asks for the first letter of the word translated

parts.note: an error is a mistake

explanation.surface: A translator first rendered the word for mistake as rogue.
explanation.definitionFit: A terror is a mischievous or troublesome person, much like a rogue or rascal.

clue.text: Lob stink bombs into test patches

indicators.note: bombs suggests the letters are blown apart and fall in a new order

explanation.surface: Pupils hurl stink bombs into an exam hall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'into' is a link; the test is the Rorschach inkblot test.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Rorschach test subjects interpret blotted ink patches, so these are test patches.

clue.text: Dance beat by lady and tramp

parts.note: to lam is to thrash or beat
Beth is a woman's name
to tramp is to walk heavily

explanation.surface: A dance rhythm is set by a woman and a vagrant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' is a link. The LAMBETH WALK is a Cockney dance of the 1930s, named after a London street.
explanation.definitionFit: The Lambeth Walk is a strutting Cockney dance made popular by a 1937 musical.

clue.text: Almost all games are so unfair

definitions.meaning: nearly every game played is something other than the bat-and-ball sport
an idiom for conduct that is unsporting or dishonourable

explanation.surface: Nearly every game is rigged against the players.
explanation.definitionFit: Calling behaviour the opposite of the English summer sport is a British idiom meaning dishonourable or unfair.

clue.text: We think no criminal informed

indicators.note: criminal suggests the letters are bent out of their lawful order

explanation.surface: We do not believe there is a criminal informer.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone in the know has inside information and is therefore informed.

clue.text: Mark's fine, holding back of twin brother

parts.note: M is an abbreviation for mark, the old German currency

indicators.note: holding says the word for fine encloses a letter

parts.note: OK means fine, all right

indicators.note: back of asks for the last letter of the word twin

explanation.surface: Mark is fine and is clinging to his twin brother.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holding' puts N, from 'back of twin', inside OK. 'Mark' and 'twin brother' suggest a person, but brother is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A monk is a member of a religious order, addressed as Brother.

clue.text: Ape, behold the man? Not half, not half

indicators.note: not half means only the front half of the Latin for behold is kept
the second not half keeps only the front half of the Latin for the man

parts.note: ecce is Latin for behold, as in Pilate's Ecce Homo
homo is Latin for man, as in Pilate's Ecce Homo

explanation.surface: Pilate's words about Christ, behold the man, are cut short, and an ape is mentioned.
explanation.walkthrough: Ecce Homo, 'behold the man', is Pilate's phrase; 'Not half, not half' halves each word, leaving EC and HO.
explanation.definitionFit: To echo someone is to ape them, repeating their words or actions.

clue.text: Tucking into booze is the ultimate in daily shame

indicators.note: tucking into says a letter is pushed inside the word for booze
the ultimate in picks out the final letter of the word for daily as the one that moves

parts.note: a daily, or char, is a British cleaning woman who comes in each day
gin is a type of booze

explanation.surface: A cleaning lady is ashamed at being caught at the gin.
explanation.walkthrough: A daily is a British cleaning woman who comes in each day. 'Tucking into' moves 'the ultimate in daily' inside the booze, leaving CHA before GRIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Chagrin is distress at having failed or been humiliated, a kind of shame.

clue.text: Lies down on this

parts.note: read as a patient lying on a couch, but meaning a drug that brings falsehoods down

explanation.surface: Someone stretches out on a bed or couch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lies' looks like a verb of reclining but is the plural noun: a drug that makes people tell the truth cuts down falsehoods.
explanation.definitionFit: A drug given to make people speak honestly reduces the falsehoods they tell.

clue.text: Odd tune qualifies to some degree

indicators.note: to some degree says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A strange melody passes muster up to a point.
explanation.definitionFit: Unequal numbers or sides fail to match, which is one sense of odd, as in an odd pair.

clue.text: Vessel just being still every second

indicators.note: every second asks for the second, fourth and so on letters of the words that follow

explanation.surface: A ship is simply lying motionless at sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'every second' takes U, T, E, N, S, I, L from 'just being still'.
explanation.definitionFit: A utensil is a household implement, and a kitchen vessel such as a pot is one.

clue.text: By Jove, I keep going round with the drinks?

definitions.text: By Jove, I keep going round with the drinks?

parts.words: By Jove, I keep going round with the drinks?
parts.note: read as a cheery exclamation from a waiter, but Jove is Jupiter: a moon circling that planet, and the cupbearer of the god

explanation.surface: A party host exclaims that they are constantly circulating with drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'By Jove' looks like an exclamation but means beside Jupiter: the moon that orbits the planet, named after the youth who served the god his drinks.
explanation.definitionFit: Ganymede was the cupbearer to Zeus, or Jove, and is also the largest moon orbiting Jupiter.

clue.text: Dismiss without second report

indicators.note: without says a letter is removed from the word for dismiss

parts.note: to cashier is to dismiss from service, especially the armed forces

explanation.surface: An officer is dismissed without getting a second report.
explanation.definitionFit: A cahier is a written report, notebook or memorandum, from the French for exercise book.

clue.text: Beat the best

definitions.meaning: to whip or whisk, as with butter and sugar in baking
the finest part, as in the pick of the crop

explanation.definitionFit: Cooks whip butter and sugar together in this way, and the finest part of anything is likewise called this.

clue.text: Reportedly excel in these with two scores

definitions.text: Reportedly excel in these with two scores

parts.words: Reportedly excel in these with two scores
parts.note: said aloud, excel sounds like the letters X and L, which together make forty, twice twenty, in the ancient numbering system

explanation.surface: Someone is said to do brilliantly in exams, getting a couple of top marks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'excel' sounds like XL, which means forty, two scores (a score is twenty), in that numbering system.
explanation.definitionFit: Roman numerals use letters for numbers, and XL among them stands for forty, two scores.

clue.text: Ruin sign when hung up

indicators.note: hung up in a down clue means the word for sign is read from bottom to top

parts.note: the Ram, Aries, is a sign of the zodiac

explanation.surface: A sign is wrecked when it is hung.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To mar something is to spoil or ruin it.

clue.text: He's again sent round back road

indicators.note: sent round says the word for again goes around the turned road abbreviation

parts.note: anew means again

indicators.note: back means the road abbreviation is read in reverse

explanation.surface: A man is again sent round by the back road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns the road abbreviation to DR. Read 'He's' as 'He is': the definition is a man's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Andrew is a man's name, so it can stand for he, a male person.

clue.text: I like odd bits of lemon cooked in oven

indicators.note: cooked suggests the letters are doctored or stewed into a new order
odd bits of asks for the first, third and fifth letters of the word lemon

explanation.surface: Someone enjoys bits of lemon baked in the oven.
explanation.walkthrough: 'odd bits of' takes L, M, N from lemon; 'cooked' mixes these with I LIKE. 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A lime kiln is a furnace for burning limestone into quicklime, a kind of industrial oven.
